What comes up in Umina Beach

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table is what the work usually involves here rather than a statement about any particular property.

Renovated house with original sheeting underneath

The commonest surprise in Umina stock, and the reason the survey comes before the quote.

How it is handled
The survey opens up the covered areas, samples are taken, and removal and clearance happen before the structure is touched.
What does it
Licensed asbestos removalists working to the survey, then the machine once cleared.

Dig in sandy ground

Quick to excavate and unwilling to stand, which changes how the face is handled.

How it is handled
Battered back or supported rather than left vertical, with the material classified before it moves.
What does it
Midi excavator with a standard bucket, tippers at the kerb.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Umina Beach

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Original fibro behind later work Very common here, where a renovation covered the sheeting rather than removing it.
  • Sandy beachside blocks Which drain well, batter poorly and behave differently from clay.
  • Flat ground with reasonable access Better than the steeper coastal suburbs nearby.
  • Steady knockdown rebuild activity On blocks that were originally holiday housing.

Umina Beach is flat with a regular street grid, so access is generally the easiest on this part of the coast. The ground is the variable: sand is quick to dig and will not hold a vertical face, so anything deep is battered or supported.

Umina Beach questions

What people ask before we start

The house was renovated years ago. Could there still be asbestos?
Frequently, yes. Renovations often covered original material rather than removing it, so eaves, sheeting and wet area linings can still be in place behind newer work. The survey opens up what a visual inspection cannot reach.
Can the slab stay?
Only if the new design allows it. Sometimes a slab stays and is built over and sometimes it all comes out, and it is cheaper to settle with your builder before the quote than halfway through.
Why is asbestos such a feature of Central Coast work?
Because a great deal of the older housing is pre 1990 fibro, much of it holiday era stock that was never replaced. Identification sits at the front of most jobs here for that reason.
Is Max licensed for the asbestos removal itself?
Max holds the demolition licence, AD214737. The asbestos removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the air monitoring and clearance by an independent licensed assessor. The whole pathway is managed as one job so you are not coordinating three contractors.
